title: Parsnip and sprout hash with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Every ingredient is a whole, everyday food, with no jars, stock pots or packet products.

supermarket.reason: Potatoes, parsnips, sprouts, red onion, eggs, butter, thyme and smoked paprika are all cheap Tesco staples in December.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large lidded frying pan and simple frying, well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: Covering the diced roots for 12 minutes, then frying uncovered for 8, cooks them through and crisps them, and four eggs over about 1.1kg of veg feeds four at lunch.

honest_times.reason: 18 minutes is fair for peeling and dicing the roots, slicing an onion and shredding 200g of sprouts, and the cook steps add up to exactly 27 minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm parsnip and sprout hash suits a cold week before Christmas, and parsnip leads the title and the pan.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Root veg, sprouts and an egg each make a filling, balanced lunch that a family would cook again.
